Suit fabric is bagged and creased: loose horizontal folds at the elbows, waist and thighs; only the knees and boots are dirt-darkened. Grey overshoes, feet apart, one foot ahead. title: Astronaut Edwin Aldrin prepares to deploy EASEP on surface of moon
camera_perspective: pure rear view, eye-level, walking away, full body, carrying two packages
visible_characteristics: Exact REAR view, camera at about chest height, subject about 6 m away walking away. The PLSS back is a two-stage white box: a smaller upper block carrying a US flag patch and a thin dark antenna rod, a larger lower block with a NASA meatball patch, two vertical columns of tan Velcro strips, a small label and an oval opening. Legs are straight, white, with mild creases behind the knees; overshoes grey with whitish dust on the edges. He carries a package in each hand with the arms held out from the body: at viewer's left a light blue-white open framework with perforated bars tilted outward, at viewer's right a grey-white box with a rod/handle protruding upward. NASA says the PSEP is in the left hand and the LRRR in the right hand, which matches that arrangement as seen from behind. A shadow stretches to the right; black sky; level horizon. The dust spray that ALSJ describes in front of the left boot is not clearly resolved in my downscaled view.
scientific_relevance: Rear silhouette and PLSS detail; the packages are the EASEP PSEP and the Laser Ranging Retroreflector in transport form.
production_influence: Rear view reference (the film has no rear shot planned; keep it in the pose library as a hidden-overlap check). Shows the PLSS back detail needed if the camera ever sees him walk away.
notes: ALSJ caption (opened): 'the piece of equipment in his right hand is the LRRR, while the seismometer package is in his left'; 'note the spray of dust spreading out in front of his left boot'; OPS antenna seen edge-on. This is the only frame found that shows the LRRR in its carried/stowed form. True frame ID: AS11-40-5942.

source_org: NASA / Apollo 11 (photographed by Neil Armstrong per NASA caption)
title: Astronaut Edwin Aldrin after deployment of EASEP on surface of moon
camera_perspective: rear three-quarter from behind-right, walking away, left of frame; LRRR small in the mid-distance
visible_characteristics: Astronaut at left of frame walking away, seen from behind and to the right, with his head turned toward the LM; the PLSS back with a flag patch is bright, the helmet cover white. Legs mid-step. Centre foreground: the passive seismometer, a copper-coloured cylinder with silvery solar-panel wings and a tilted mast. Right: the LM with gold foil and a leg; a distant flag at the horizon; small white objects beyond the seismometer (the NASA caption identifies the Laser Ranging Retro-Reflector beyond the seismometer; I cropped it separately). Regolith covered in bootprints; horizon at about 43 percent of frame height; black sky.
scientific_relevance: Layout of the EASEP site; the LRRR is far smaller than the seismometer's mast and lower than the astronaut's knee.
production_influence: Shows the true relative scale and low height of the array against the astronaut (array roughly knee height or below), and the rear 3/4 walking gait.
notes: Caption in NASA record: 'beyond [the PSEP] is the Laser Ranging Retro-Reflector (LR-3)'. Manifest cites this frame; its identity and content are confirmed. Cropped detail of the LRRR is in research/real_world_references/reflector/. True frame ID: AS11-40-5948.

title: Astronaut Edwin Aldrin deploying Solar Wind Composition experiment
camera_perspective: rear three-quarter from the astronaut's right-back, striding forward with a tool
visible_characteristics: Rear three-quarter view from behind-right at about 3 m. The PLSS is a flat white box: smaller upper block with a US flag patch, larger lower block with a NASA patch and tan Velcro strips, a small oval opening, an antenna stub on top. A white corrugated hose loops from the chest unit around the right hip to the PLSS. Helmet seen from behind with the visor edge at the front. Wide stride: left leg back with the boot on its toe and heel lifted, right boot forward, torso inclined forward. His right hand grips a horizontal handle bar of a thin silver pole standing vertically in the soil; behind it a tall pole with a silver foil sheet and a red-capped top (the SWC). Boots grey, ridged, lower legs lightly dust-grey; deep herringbone bootprints in dark disturbed soil.

title: Apollo 11 Mission image - Astronaut Edwin Aldrin descends the Lunar Module ladder

visible_characteristics: Seen from behind and below as the astronaut hops down to the ladder: the right leg is swung back with the sole facing the lens, a smooth flat pale blue-grey slab with a raised rim and no tread visible; the left boot is on or near the top rung. The PLSS top (flag patch) is a box above the shoulders; his left arm reaches to a handrail with a glove and a dark wrist cuff. White suit with loose creases on the thighs; lower legs and overshoes grey. LM foil in gold, copper and black fills the frame; black sky; grey regolith at the lower left; the UNITED STATES lettering at right.

title: Astronaut Charles Conrad during extravehicular activity on lunar surface
camera_perspective: front close-up, waist down, standing on boulder-strewn regolith
visible_characteristics: Black and white, waist down, standing on boulder-strewn regolith. The glove at viewer's left holds the handle of a long rod with a lanyard; the rod runs to the ground and ends in a multi-tined head (the tongs/rake type tool) resting on the surface. The other glove hangs open and relaxed. Both gloves are dark with dust. Thigh pockets with flaps and a patch; knees and shins show thick accordion convolutions that are grey with dust; boot overshoes are heavy, ridged and dark. Wide stance, knees slightly flexed; a sharp shadow cuts across the soil.
scientific_relevance: Real glove, knee and boot construction and how dust sticks to it.
production_influence: Gloves are bulky, tapered, with dark dust-stained palms; boots are thick and rounded with a ridged ankle band; lower legs should be dust-grey, upper body clean (Apollo 11 and 12 look).
notes: Apollo 12 suit is the same A7L family as Apollo 11. NASA caption: tongs (ALHT) in the right hand; lunar soil on the suit around the knees and below; EVA checklist on the left wrist (cut off at the top of the frame). True frame ID: AS12-48-7149.

title: Astronaut Alan Bean with subpackages of the ALSEP during EVA

The astronaut walks toward the camera carrying two ALSEP packages, one hanging at each end of a bar at hip height, arms spread out. Visor dark; chest hardware. A low, bright haze of dust surrounds both boots; it lies flat near the ground (about shin height) and shows no tall column. title: Astronaut Charles Duke photographed collecting lunar samples at Station 1

title: Time-of-flight ranging diagram with d = c t / 2
camera_perspective: 2-D schematic, emitter at left, target at right
visible_characteristics: Pale mint-green panel. At the left an emitter (grey box with a tan lens) drawn twice: solid at the top, ghosted lower with a small camera-like receiver solid at the bottom, joined by a bold downward arrow and a vertical double-headed dimension line labelled 'time t' (rotated, bold italic). A thick bright-yellow band runs from the emitter to a bullseye target (blue plate, black-and-white rings, red centre) at the right, and a second yellow band returns from the target to the receiver, forming a V on its side. Each band has a thin arrow and a small wave-packet squiggle marking the pulse. A horizontal double-headed dimension line across the top labelled 'distance d'. Bottom right: 'd = ct/2' as a stacked fraction in bold italic serif.
scientific_relevance: Exactly the Slot 07 relation C11: time axis, out-and-back path, distance bracket and the divide-by-two fraction in one picture.
production_influence: B33-B36: keep three separate marks - a time bracket (t), the total path bar, and the one-way distance bracket (d) - and show the V (out leg, back leg offset) before folding it into one leg on '/2'. Wave-packet glyph inside the band is a ready symbol for a pulse.

title: Moon's distance range to scale, with a 1-light-second bar
camera_perspective: strip diagram, Earth at left, scale in km, rendered to a 1600 px PNG by me
visible_characteristics: White background; wide horizontal strip. Earth as a blue ball at far left with three thin concentric rings labelled ISS (magenta), GPS (lilac) and GEO (green). Two rulers: 'Distance from Earth centre' (0 to 400 000 km, ticks every 50 000 km) above and 'Distance from Earth surface' below. Between them a long slim yellow wedge from Earth to the Moon's three positions, three black spheres marking min., mean and max. near 360 000, 384 000 and 405 000 km, with the apparent angular sizes 33.5' (red) and 29.43' (gold). A blue bar labelled '1 light-second' spans about three quarters of the way to the Moon. Magenta bars 'ISS orbit length' mark the size of the ISS orbit at the near and far ends.
scientific_relevance: Shows the range of the Earth-Moon distance on one ruler and how long 1 light-second is against it (C03).
production_influence: B10/B12: add a light-second bar to the ruler: the pulse covers the bar in 1 s and a little more than the bar (1.28x) to reach the Moon. Min/mean/max ticks give B12's ruler its anchors.
notes: SVG declared 4215x562; my render is a 1600 px square with the strip centred, small text only legible at full zoom.

title: Full Moon at perigee vs apogee
camera_perspective: two full-Moon photographs side by side at the same scale
visible_characteristics: Black background. Two grey full-Moon discs: the left larger, titled 'Lunar perigee (33.48 [arcmin mark])  (356,700 km)  2007 Oct 26 12:02:39 UT', the right smaller, titled 'Lunar Apogee (29.40 [arcmin mark])  (406,300 km)  2007 Apr 3 08:50:54 UT'. Thin white construction lines run from the top of the left disc across, and a vertical white bracket with the label '12% smaller' at the lower right marks the difference in diameter. Craters and maria identical on both (same photo scaled).

production_influence: B13: beside the timer (2.38 s near / 2.71 s far) show two Moon discs differing by ~12% with the same bracket device. Label caveat: these distances are two specific 2007 events, not the ledger extremes; do not cite its numbers.
notes: The angular size marks read 33.48 and 29.40 with an inch-like quote mark in the image (arcminutes in the original); I transcribed what is shown.

title: Earth-Moon distance over 700 days (plot)
camera_perspective: line chart, white background, grey gridlines
visible_characteristics: Title 'Distance Earth - Moon'. X axis 'Days' 0-700 with gridlines every 100 days; Y axis 'Distance Earth - Moon, km' from 340000 to 440000 (gridlines every 20000). A thick black oscillating curve with about 25 cycles of period near 27.5 days. Peaks (apogees) mostly 404 000-406 500 km, troughs (perigees) vary more widely, between about 356 500 and 370 000 km. The envelope itself drifts: the amplitude is not constant cycle to cycle.
scientific_relevance: The monthly extremes vary; the 'about 357 000 to 407 000 km' ledger range is the envelope of many months.
production_influence: B12: the ruler's live value should follow a non-constant amplitude rather than a perfect sine between fixed limits, or accept the simple version with the exaggerated-ellipse disclosure.
notes: The data source and epoch of the plot are not stated in the file; I read values off the axes by eye.

title: Earth-Moon distance and Moon phase through a year (chart)
camera_perspective: chart on white, then black padding
visible_characteristics: A single-frame chart (ffprobe reports one frame, so it is static, not animated). Top 215 px: white plot with left axis 'Distance [km]' 350 000 to 410 000, a black sinusoidal curve with about 13 cycles between roughly 357 000 and 406 000 km, a pale grey saw-tooth for Moon phase with right axis 0 to 1, and month labels Jan-Dec along the bottom. The rest of the canvas is black.
scientific_relevance: Distance and phase cycles are different: phase and distance repeat at different periods.
production_influence: Do not tie the distance animation to phase in B12/B13 (the film does not show phases at all).

title: Earth and Moon: speed of light in real time (animation)
camera_perspective: animated strip, Earth left, Moon right, black ground
visible_characteristics: Frames sampled (126 frames at 50 fps, 2.52 s; eight tiles every 6 frames). Black strip with small stars. Heading 'Speed of light in real-time / Surface-to-surface in 1.255 seconds'. A small Earth globe at far left, a small grey Moon dot at far right, labels EARTH and MOON in small caps beneath each, a thin white dimension line between them with the text 'Average distance 384,400 KM' beneath it. A white glowing pulse starts at Earth's right edge as a point and, as it travels, stretches into a horizontal ellipse (motion-blurred glow) heading to the Moon. No ticks or counters.
scientific_relevance: A real-time light crossing of the Earth-Moon gap: 1.255 s surface to surface, 384,400 km centre to centre (1.282 s).
production_influence: B10/B11: show the pulse as a soft stretched glow with a dimension line underneath; the spoken '1.28 s' is centre-to-centre; if the artwork shows surface-to-surface spacing the true crossing is 1.255 s (I compute 376,292 km / c = 1.2552 s). Decide which and label it.
credit_line: Dr. James O'Donoghue (YouTube alias Interplanetary) / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0
notes: Animation reviewed as FRAME_SAMPLED, not watched.

title: Earth orbit classes with the lunar orbit as an arc
camera_perspective: 2-D schematic, Earth at left, 720x240
visible_characteristics: White background. A small dark Earth circle at left with a thin red ring, inside a large pale-pink disc. Three leader lines with bold labels: 'low Earth orbit (180-2,000 km)', 'mid Earth orbit (2,000-35,780 km)', 'high Earth & geosynchronous orbit (>=35,780 km)'. At the right edge a large thin red arc with a black dot labelled 'lunar orbit (384,000 km)'. Earth is not to scale against the lunar arc.
scientific_relevance: Simple labelling pattern for the Earth-Moon gap vs near-Earth orbits (NASA graphic).
production_influence: B05/B12: a leader-line label style (bold label, thin line) works at small sizes; the lunar orbit is shown as a single arc, not an ellipse.

title: Radar operation animation: pulse out, echo back, timer and scope
camera_perspective: animated, side-on schematic
visible_characteristics: Frames sampled (44 frames, 3.1 s; 11 tiles). Pale lavender background. Left: a radar dish on a lattice tower on a ground line; top-left: a round stopwatch icon whose red pie wedge fills clockwise as time elapses; top-right: an aeroplane (target). A small blue square leaves the dish and grows as it rises toward the aircraft; when it reaches the aircraft a cyan ring bursts at the target and an expanding cyan arc travels back toward the dish. Bottom right: a dark-green scope window with a thin green trace and one spike that moves along the baseline as the echo returns.
scientific_relevance: Out-and-back pulse tied to a running timer and a distance trace: the same story as B05-B11.
production_influence: B06-B11: a pie wedge filling on the stopwatch icon is a clear elapsed-time cue; pulse out and echo back in different colours (blue square / cyan ring) supports the warm/cool grammar.
credit_line: Averse (de.wikipedia) / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 DE
notes: Animation reviewed as FRAME_SAMPLED. Tiny (340x140).

title: Earth and Moon (to-scale and 5x oversize orbit visualisation)
camera_perspective: top-down from the north ecliptic pole

title: View of the Earth seen by the Apollo 17 crew traveling toward the moon (AS17-148-22727)
camera_perspective: full sunlit disc, south at bottom, translunar coast (tens of thousands of km)
visible_characteristics: Fully lit, almost circular disc on pure black, nearly centred, no other objects. Large swirls of white cloud over the southern oceans and cloud bands over central Africa. The limb is sharp with a slightly paler, thin blue-white rim; no visible glow halo outside the disc. Sun is behind the camera so there is no terminator and the lighting is flat; brightness falls off slightly at the edge. Clouds are bright pure white with soft edges and visible spiral structure (frontal systems).
scientific_relevance: Canonical full-disc look: blue ocean, orange-brown deserts, white clouds, thin limb. South-up/south-bottom orientation shows Antarctica as a white cap, not a flat white blob.
production_influence: Colour target for the Earth globe: ocean deep blue (not cyan), land ochre/brown/green, clouds pure white with soft alpha, limb rim thin and pale blue. Clouds cover roughly half the disc, so cloud alpha should be dense, not sprinkled.

A thin dark-blue halo ring surrounds the whole disc outside the limb (a soft glow a few pixels wide). Several vertical pale grey streaks are visible, mostly across the lower half, where the orbit swaths of the composite do not match; the limb is darker and bluer than the centre. This is a data composite with no true terminator.

title: From a Million Miles Away, NASA Camera Shows Moon Crossing Face of Earth
camera_perspective: full disc seen from the Sun-Earth L1 point (about a million miles per caption); Moon lies between camera and Earth
visible_characteristics: Full sunlit disc of Earth, Americas near the top centre, cyclone and ocean cloud swirls in the Pacific. The far side of the Moon covers a lower-left part of the disc as a dark grey-brown disc with faint ray streaks and a few dark craters, with a thin green fringe on its right edge (colour-channel misregistration from the camera's exposures). The Moon is clearly less bright than the Earth. Measured on the displayed image: Earth about 1485 px wide, Moon about 540 px wide, ratio about 0.36.
scientific_relevance: Real example of Earth and Moon in one frame. The apparent size ratio is 0.36, larger than the true 0.2727, because the Moon is much closer to this camera than the Earth is (perspective).
production_influence: Shows that Earth is much brighter than the Moon (Earth geometric albedo 0.434 vs Moon 0.12 in the NASA fact sheets): when both appear in one frame keep the Earth visibly brighter and bluer. Warns that any perspective frame with the Moon nearer to the camera must not use the 0.2727 ratio.
notes: Original 2048x2048 PNG, 3.27 MB, saved unscaled. Green edge fringe is an instrument artefact. Saved file 2048x2048, 3267769 bytes.

title: Artemis Era Earthrise (art002e009280)

visible_characteristics: Portrait frame, Earth is a narrow crescent: lit limb on the right, a curved terminator on the left, with the unlit side invisible. The straight right-hand edge of the lit shape is a hard vertical cut most likely where the spacecraft window or frame clipped the view; it is not a physical shape. Horns of the crescent taper to fine points that extend slightly beyond the terminator curve. The surface near the terminator is dimmed yellowish-beige by sunset/twilight light.

production_influence: If a crescent Earth is shown, use warm (yellowish) tinting along the last few percent before the terminator. Do not reproduce the straight clipped edge. Crescent horns must taper to fine points.

title: APOLLO XIV - CREW TRAINING - KSC
camera_perspective: rear 3/4 (near figure) and profile walking (far figure), outdoor eye-level, hardware on the ground
visible_characteristics: Colour outdoor training photo (Kennedy Space Center, pale sand, scrub and a palm in the background). Left astronaut seen from the REAR, slightly 3/4 to the right: PLSS with NASA logo and vent grilles, flag patch on the top pack, antenna; helmet with side visor shade. Second astronaut in profile walking left with red arm and leg stripes (commander markings), bag-like tool in hand, next to an ALSEP-like central station with gold foil and a rover trainer behind. Orange-gold ribbon cables lie in radial lines on the ground. Some other hardware (a cylinder, black panel, white box) is scattered around.
scientific_relevance: Rear view of PLSS with NASA logo, vent grilles and top pack, plus a figure walking beside deployed ALSEP-type hardware.
production_influence: Rear/back 3/4 reference for the PLSS back plate, antenna and the way the helmet sits relative to the pack from behind; useful only if a back view is ever needed (currently NOT PLANNED).
notes: TRAINING photograph at Kennedy Space Center (sand site), not the Moon. Suit and pack are Apollo-14-era; commander stripes on the far figure. Caption (not verified): Apollo 14 crew ALSEP training.

title: KSC-71pc-0470
camera_perspective: pure side view, eye-level to slightly low, medium shot, bending forward carrying an instrument box
visible_characteristics: Colour, medium shot, outdoor training with orange-brown soil. Central astronaut is in a clean PURE SIDE view (facing left), bent forward at the waist about 30-40 degrees with knees flexed, holding a white bag-like instrument box with the right glove and a rod in the left; PLSS backplate with straps, flag patch on the shoulder, helmet with a side-visible face through the visor; boots with blue-grey soles. A second astronaut with a gold visor stands further back in front view. Hardware on the ground at left with orange ribbons. Hard sun shadow on the soil.
scientific_relevance: Side view of a forward-bent walking pose with a load in the glove.
production_influence: Side-profile bend reference with the A7LB-type suit: shows PLSS tilting with the spine, belt/strap detail and boot shape; pairs with S69-32233 for the bend range.
notes: TRAINING photograph at KSC with Hadley-like terrain mock-up; A7LB (Apollo 15+) suit. Caption (not verified): Irwin deploys the Suprathermal Ion Detector Experiment, Scott in the background.

title: KSC-AS11-40-5951
camera_perspective: front 3/4 from the astronaut's left, eye-level, mid-distance, on the real lunar surface
visible_characteristics: Real Apollo 11 surface photo (grainy scan of a print with registration crosses). Astronaut stands upper-left, seen 3/4 from the front/left, torso slightly forward, holding a long grey extension handle that reaches down to the copper-gold cylindrical top of the seismometer package; the chest remote control unit and hose connectors are sharp; the gold visor reflects the sunlit scene and shows a hint of the face; PLSS edge behind. In the foreground the package has two dark solar-panel wings on the left and a reflective flat sheet array on the right; bootprints with chevron tread in the bottom right; boulder-strewn dark grey regolith; sun from the left; black sky over a close horizon.
scientific_relevance: Real EVA equipment alignment: the astronaut uses a long handle to point and level a deployed instrument (the same job as aligning a reflector).
production_influence: Only real-surface photo of an astronaut interacting with a deployed package by tool: slight stoop, handle at 45 degrees to the ground, both gloves on equipment. Use it for the arm/handle geometry of the align beat; the kneel itself is still stylised.
notes: Scan of a print (grain, registration crosses). The object is the Passive Seismic Experiment (PSEP) per the caption and ALSJ, NOT the retroreflector. Caption of ALSJ (index page read): Buzz is adjusting pointing and levelling with the handle. Observed in the image: copper-coloured cylinder, two solar-panel wings, chevron bootprints.

title: Crop of AS11-40-5903 (head and visor)
camera_perspective: front, eye-level, tight head and shoulders crop (native pixels, 1150x1050) of AS11-40-5903
visible_characteristics: Close crop of the head/upper chest from AS11-40-5903 (native resolution crop, 1150x1050): white helmet shell cover with creased, quilted-looking top, buckles/snap fasteners on the pressure-helmet sides and a loose cloth neck/shoulder area; the gold-coated outer visor is a near-opaque mirror showing a bright regolith foreground, a long cast shadow with a registration cross, the LM with gold foil and one standing figure plus two small poles; the black rim of the visor assembly and a thin white neck ring below; US flag patch on the shoulder; top of the chest remote-control unit with a name tag. No face is visible.
scientific_relevance: The visor is a near-opaque gold mirror that reflects the surroundings; it is the standard way astronauts are identified without their faces.
production_influence: CLOSE HELMET REFERENCE (fills the gap of ASTRO_001 having only full-body shots): quilted helmet cover with fasteners, visor opening with a dark seal ring, neck ring and collar; the visor reflection plate (ASTRO_003) is an inverted fisheye of a bright foreground, a long dark cast shadow, the LM with gold foil and a small standing figure.
notes: DERIVED CROP of REF-ASTRO-001 original (source frame AS11-40-5903, sha256 of the original frame is given). Crop box 2100,0 to 3250,1050 of the 5189x5067 original. Registration cross visible in the visor. A name tag is visible at the bottom edge: do not copy lettering.

title: Crop of AS11-40-5903 (chest unit, hoses and glove)
camera_perspective: front, eye-level, torso and right glove crop (native pixels, 1250x1100) of AS11-40-5903
visible_characteristics: Close crop of torso from AS11-40-5903 (1250x1100): chest remote-control unit (white fabric box with a gold latch plate, switches and a label OFF/MAIN/MOM/TALK, a name tag on the left edge and a small mission patch), blue and red/orange hose connectors with metal fittings, white fabric straps, dust-streaked suit fabric with soft wrinkles; the right gloved hand is dirty grey with a blue-grey fingertip and a quilted wrist cuff; flag patch on the upper arm; lunar surface behind.
scientific_relevance: Chest remote-control unit, gas/water hose connectors and the dust-stained glove.
production_influence: Close torso/glove reference: RCU is a fabric-covered box with a gold latch plate and switches, connector fittings are blue and red/orange, straps are cream webbing; the glove is a dusty grey-brown mitten with a blue-grey fingertip cap and a quilted wrist ring. Use for ASTRO_004/007 detail.
notes: DERIVED CROP of AS11-40-5903 (crop box 2250,650 to 3500,1750 of the 5189x5067 original). Name tag and label lettering are visible: do not copy.

title: Astronaut David Scott on slope of Hadley Delta during Apollo 15 EVA
camera_perspective: rear 3/4, eye-level-ish, wide shot; astronaut small at upper left on a slope, rover at right
visible_characteristics: B/W Apollo 15 frame with registration crosses. A small astronaut at upper left on a long smooth slope, seen from the REAR-3/4, bent forward at the waist with knees flexed and one arm reaching down to a boulder with tongs/gnomon; the PLSS and OPS pack are visible from behind. The sun is low: the astronaut's shadow stretches roughly 3-4 body-lengths to the right across the dust. At right foreground the Lunar Roving Vehicle seen from the front-left with its umbrella-like high-gain antenna, flag on the fender, and wire-mesh wheel. Black sky over a smooth hill horizon; fine-grained dust with crisp boot/tyre tracks.
scientific_relevance: Real EVA stooping to reach a boulder with tongs; a long cast shadow on dust under a low Sun.
production_influence: Shows the full-body bend-and-reach silhouette from behind on the real surface, and that the cast shadow is a distorted long silhouette (about 3-4 body lengths) for ASTRO_011/RETRO_006; the horizon is a smooth hill line against pure black.
notes: Astronaut is small in the frame (about 1/6 of frame height) so suit detail is thin. Registration crosses are scanner/camera reseau marks. Caption (not verified): Scott with tongs and gnomon studies a boulder on Hadley Delta.

title: Astronaut David Scott on slope of Hadley Delta during Apollo 15 EVA
camera_perspective: rear-right 3/4, eye-level, large in frame; torso turned, helmet in near profile, holding a camera
visible_characteristics: B/W Apollo 15 frame with heavy artefacts (two bright blobs in the upper sky, hazy upper area, grain): large astronaut seen from the REAR-RIGHT 3/4, turned toward a camera, helmet turned in near profile with the gold visor reflecting a small figure and sun glare; PLSS and OPS box with antenna dominate his back; suit is heavily dust-stained on legs and lower arms (light grey tone); the right arm holds a 70 mm camera at chest height. A long soft shadow trails to the lower left; rolling round hills behind, rover in the background and a tripod-like gnomon/pole at right. A tiny dust puff is visible near the foot.
asset_ids: ASTRO_001_HELMET ASTRO_002_VISOR ASTRO_005_PLSS ASTRO_006_ARMS ASTRO_010_POSE_SET ASTRO_011_SHADOW
scientific_relevance: Real EVA rear 3/4 of the PLSS/OPS pack with the helmet turned: visor seen from the side with a reflected figure.
production_influence: Best REAL rear-3/4 reference with the helmet turned to near-profile: PLSS+OPS pack mass dominates the back, helmet sits forward of the pack, and the whole suit is dust-grey below the waist.
notes: The frame has strong artefacts (two bright blobs and hazy sky at the top, grain): treat as photographic defects, not scene content. Caption (not verified): Scott uses a 70 mm camera on the Hadley Delta slope.

title: Astronaut James Irwin gives salute beside U.S. flag during EVA
camera_perspective: front 3/4, eye-level, astronaut at left of frame, LM and rover behind
visible_characteristics: Colour Apollo 15: astronaut at left standing front 3/4, one arm raised to the visor in a salute, gold visor dark with a faint reflection, A7LB suit with dust-grey legs and lighter torso; behind him a rippling US flag on a pole, the LM descent stage wrapped in gold and black foil and the LRV at right with its mesh dish; a large smooth mountain behind and black sky. Foreground regolith covered in boot prints (chevron tread) and a long hard shadow of the flag running to the right.
scientific_relevance: A7LB suit standing with an arm raised to the visor; also shows hard sun, boot prints and the LM/rover scale.
production_influence: Lower priority: another standing front-3/4 (already covered by ASTRO-001/002). Useful only for the A7LB colour split (lighter torso, dust-grey legs) and for the raised-arm silhouette.
notes: Largely redundant with REF-ASTRO-001/002 for stance; kept for the visor-with-raised-arm and the LM/LRV scene context. Caption (not verified): Irwin salutes beside the flag.

title: Earth Observations taken by the Expedition 23 Crew
camera_perspective: edge-on limb (horizon tangent) from low Earth orbit, tilted across the frame
visible_characteristics: Edge-on limb view tilted diagonally across the frame: black space at top fading through deep blue and a bright pale-blue band to a thin white-cream layer, then a saturated orange-yellow band right at the horizon, with a very thin dark layer between the white and orange bands; below the horizon the Earth is almost black with only faint cloud silhouettes. No visible sun disc. Colour is stacked horizontal bands with soft transitions; a text label ISS023E057948 is burned into a white strip at the bottom.
scientific_relevance: Atmosphere seen edge-on: stacked colour layers (orange troposphere, white/cream, blue stratosphere/mesosphere, black space) over a very thin shell.
production_influence: Defines the atmosphere limb slice (EARTH_003 limb ramp and EARTH_006 side cross-section): bands are soft-edged horizontal gradients; total visible thickness is a very thin fraction of the globe radius; no hard outline.
notes: Caption (not verified): sunset over the Indian Ocean; layers roughly denote atmospheric layers. A frame-ID label strip is burned into the bottom of the image: crop it off.

title: Earth Observations
camera_perspective: near-horizontal limb at orbital twilight, straight-on
visible_characteristics: Nearly horizontal limb at twilight: black at top, a faint streaky electric-blue thin layer (noctilucent/polar mesospheric clouds, per caption) high above, a smooth blue-to-cyan-to-intense white band, then a thin orange line exactly on the horizon with an orange glow on the lower right where the sun is just below. The ground below is dark blue-grey with a warm glow; two small dark smudges (sensor/window dust) are visible. Frame ID label in white strip at bottom.
scientific_relevance: Thin high-altitude noctilucent cloud layer above a white airglow/twilight band and an orange horizon line.
production_influence: Shows the limb as a straight-on horizontal band structure: dark sky, a faint streaky electric-blue thin layer, a bright white/cyan band and a thin orange line at the horizon; no curved limb in this crop. Use for a dawn/dusk limb variant of EARTH_003 and the high thin layer.
notes: Caption (not verified): polar mesospheric clouds lit by an orbital sunrise. Two dark smudges are dust on the lens/window: artefacts. Frame-ID strip at the bottom.

title: Sunrise, Earth Limb, SW Pacific Ocean
camera_perspective: edge-on limb, tilted, with silhouetted cumulus in the foreground and a sun glint
visible_characteristics: Edge-on orbital sunrise/sunset limb tilted across the frame: black sky; a thin faint blue layer high up, a brilliant white-lilac band, then a dark gap, then a broad orange band fading to red at lower left; a bright sun glint low in the centre breaks through silhouetted dark cumulus clouds in the foreground; a tiny bright spot at upper left (a star/planet or spacecraft). The Earth below the horizon is solid black.
scientific_relevance: Limb layers (blue, white, orange) plus cloud tops silhouetted at the horizon line.
production_influence: Shows clouds as a thin textured layer on the globe edge: dark silhouettes with bright rim light against the orange band; use for the cloud edge and limb silhouette.
notes: Space Shuttle film frame; a tiny bright dot at upper left (star, planet or spacecraft) is unexplained: not identified from the picture. Caption (not verified): sunrise over the south-west Pacific Ocean.

title: Earth Observation
camera_perspective: oblique limb view at night from the ISS with robot arm and solar array in the frame
visible_characteristics: Wide limb view at night from the ISS: black star-filled sky, a thin green-olive airglow/aurora band lying above a thin blue rim and a bright white-blue cloud deck lit by moonlight; clouds in the lower right look like cumulus cells over dark ocean; at lower left a dark landmass with a few small orange city lights. The Canadarm2-type robotic arm (cream thermal wraps) hangs in a V across the centre and orange solar array blades occupy the right edge; ISS modules at the top. Clouds are lit blue-white from above, giving an obvious thin cloud layer sitting on the globe surface.
scientific_relevance: Night-side Earth: moonlit cloud deck as a thin bright layer, airglow band above the limb, a few city lights on dark land.
production_influence: Shows the nightside look for B37-style shots: clouds are blue-white from moonlight, the rim is a thin blue edge capped by an olive-green airglow band, city lights are tiny orange dots (not a continuous glow); includes ISS hardware that must be left out.
notes: Caption (not verified): HDR night series, New Zealand pass; aurora visible over limb. I saw an olive/green band and orange lights but cannot confirm they are aurora vs airglow.

title: Earth Observations taken by the Expedition 35 Crew
camera_perspective: near-nadir night view of a dense urban region from the ISS
visible_characteristics: Straight-down night view of a dense urban area: orange-yellow sodium lights tracing roads in thin branching lines and filling suburbs as glowing patches; several brighter white cores at city centres; black dark gaps (fields/water); some pinpoint blue-white lights. No visible coastline or clouds; slight grain. Caption gives no place name.
scientific_relevance: What city lights look like from orbit: orange road lines, sodium-lit suburbs, small white cores.
production_influence: Texture reference for the night-lights layer close-up: light is mostly thin orange lines and patches with sharp black gaps, not blobs; cores are small and white; maintain the colour split orange vs white.
notes: Caption gives no place name; none is claimed. Slight sensor grain.

title: Earth Observation
camera_perspective: oblique night view of a large grid city between dark mountains
visible_characteristics: Oblique night view of a large grid-pattern city sitting between dark mountain ranges: orange street grids, brighter white lights at the dense centre, and soft haze/glow lifting off the urban area; a dark patch (sea or cloud) at the upper right. Folder note in the caption says California. Colour is warm orange on near-black.
scientific_relevance: Oblique city-light grid with scattered haze glow and a dark sea/cloud patch.
production_influence: Shows the glow-above-city haze and the grid structure; useful to set a modest bloom radius for the night-lights layer.
notes: Caption folder note says California (not verified from the picture).

title: "Aurora Australis, Airglow, Terminator  view taken by the Expedition 29 crew"
camera_perspective: oblique night limb view with aurora below the horizon line and ISS truss in the corner
visible_characteristics: Night limb view: black star-filled sky; a curved horizon with a thin brownish-tan airglow band hugging the limb, a dull red glow above it in the centre, and vivid green aurora curtains and rays spreading across the surface below the horizon, with thin vertical streaks rising at left. Dark ISS solar-array/truss structure fills the upper-left corner. NO terminator is visible despite the title word; the unlit Earth surface itself appears veiled green by aurora.
scientific_relevance: Night limb: airglow band along the horizon and aurora curtains over the surface.
production_influence: Shows the night limb rim colour (tan/brown airglow thin band, dull red glow) as opposed to the blue daylight rim; use only as a colour-negative example (the film shows no aurora).
notes: Title says terminator but NO terminator is visible in the picture (checked). Low production value; keep only as a night-rim colour reference.

title: Thunderstorms over the Pacific Ocean as seen from STS-64
camera_perspective: oblique daytime view toward the limb at high altitude, square 70 mm frame
visible_characteristics: Oblique daytime view toward the horizon (square 70 mm frame): black space at top, a thin bright blue atmospheric layer above the limb, then a field of white cumulus and cumulonimbus clouds over dark blue ocean. Towers with cauliflower tops cast long dark shadows on the cloud deck and sea; low sun from the left/back produces strong relief; a flatter cream-coloured high haze/cloud sheet near the horizon. Cloud clumps recede in perspective toward the limb, showing clouds as a thin layer sitting on the globe.
scientific_relevance: Clouds as a thin layer on the globe: towering cumulus casting long shadows on a lower cloud deck and dark sea, with a blue rim at the horizon.
production_influence: Cloud-layer reference with height cues: cloud tops are bright white, shadows are dark blue; clouds shrink to thin textured bands near the limb; use for the separate cloud layer (EARTH_002) with soft alpha and cast shadows only when the camera is oblique.
notes: Caption (not verified): thunderstorms about 16 degrees south-east of Hawaii.

title: NASA Satellites See Santa's North Pole
camera_perspective: straight-down polar mosaic of the Arctic (satellite swaths stitched), north pole at centre
visible_characteristics: Straight-down mosaic of the Arctic in summer: a pale blue-white sea-ice pack fills the centre with cracks and flow lines; ringed by brown-green tundra land, fjorded islands (lower-left the white Greenland ice sheet), black open water patches and swirling white cyclonic cloud systems; visible seams where separate satellite swaths join. Cloud covers perhaps 40 percent; pole region is cloud-free ice.
scientific_relevance: What the pole region actually looks like: pale sea-ice with fractures, Greenland ice sheet, tundra, open water and cloud swirls.
production_influence: Reference for repainting the grey filler band at the pole of the cloud-free map: ice is blue-white with fine crack lines and slightly darker coast margins, not flat white; Greenland sits as a bright wedge.
notes: Visible seams where swaths join and ~40 percent cloud: not a clean cloud-free map. Orthographic-polar projection, not equirectangular. Caption (not verified): Terra mosaic, summer.

title: South Polar Projection of Earth
camera_perspective: south-polar-up globe disc with no night side (composite)
visible_characteristics: Small (452x439) south-polar-up globe: white Antarctica at the centre ringed by deep blue ocean with large swirling white cloud bands spiralling clockwise; fully lit disc with no night side or terminator; black background; limb is a soft blue edge. Low resolution, some banding.
scientific_relevance: Antarctica and surrounding cloud spirals as a globe with the pole centred.
production_influence: Low-resolution (452x439) but the only globe-with-the-pole-in-view example: shows polar cloud spirals around Antarctica; use as a layout reference, not as a texture.
notes: Caption (not verified): the whole disc is lit, which is physically impossible: composite. Very small, banding visible.

title: A New View of the Moon
camera_perspective: large Moon limb with a razor-sharp edge against black, half-lit; tiny Earth crescent behind the limb
visible_characteristics: Moon limb, large: a half-lit grey globe fills the frame from the bottom with the curved limb as a sharp, perfectly clean edge against black space (no haze). Dense overlapping craters, a few large basins, lit from the top so the shadowed lower part fades to black along an irregular terminator. A tiny crescent Earth (blue-white) sits just behind the limb at upper left, almost touching it. No stars.
scientific_relevance: No atmosphere: the lunar limb is a hard edge with no haze or glow; terminator is irregular and cratered.
production_influence: Settles the Moon limb treatment for MOON_001/004: clean antialiased edge, NO rim glow, terminator follows terrain (jagged), shadowed side almost black; Earth is only a few percent of the Moon diameter here.
notes: Caption (not verified): far-side view from Artemis II, Earth sets over the limb.

title: Taking a Peek at Earth from the Far Side of the Moon
camera_perspective: very low oblique view of the lunar horizon, Earth crescent dipping behind the limb
visible_characteristics: Wide Moon limb: a very low-angle view of a heavily cratered grey surface with a sharp curved limb against black; near the top-centre a small blue-white gibbous/crescent Earth just peeks over the horizon, cut by the limb. Craters are bowl-shaped and soft-edged; surface is a uniform mid-grey with subtle shading; no atmosphere, no stars.
scientific_relevance: Shows how a surface horizon appears from orbit: hard black line, uniform mid-grey craters, no haze, no stars.
production_influence: Reference for MOON_003 horizon (black sky, sharp line, no haze) and for placing Earth on the horizon in a wide view.
notes: This is an ORBITAL view, not from the surface; surface horizon from the ground is nearer and lower-contrast to terrain.

title: Lunar Observations taken by the Expedition 39 Crew
camera_perspective: telephoto view of the Moon at the moment of setting behind the limb, from the ISS
visible_characteristics: A small, pale-blue/white Moon with faint maria, flattened into a squat dome shape (the bottom is cut flat and tinted pink-orange) by atmospheric refraction near the horizon, floating in a smooth vertical gradient from dark navy at top to brighter blue at the bottom (the airglow/atmosphere seen from orbit). No Earth surface or spacecraft in the frame.
scientific_relevance: Atmospheric refraction squashes the Moon vertically and reddens its lower edge; background is the airglow/atmosphere gradient.
production_influence: Useful ONLY for the lunar-sky-through-air idea (B01): the Moon shape flattens near the horizon; the film Moon should be round when high in the sky.
notes: Caption (not verified): moonset with airglow in view.

title: Astronaut David Scott on slope of Hadley Delta during Apollo 15 EVA
camera_perspective: ground-level wide view over sunlit dust to a shadowed slope and a far ridge, rover at left
visible_characteristics: B/W Apollo 15 frame: very hard-lit terrain. Foreground dust with many small crisp dark shadows and footprints; mid-ground a sunlit smooth hill on the left and a huge pitch-black shadowed slope in the centre (no fill light at all); a long ridge horizon against black sky with a tiny peak at right. The astronaut at the rover (left centre) is small, seen from the rear/3-4, leaning on the rover; the LRV is seen from the rear-left with its dish antenna folded out.
scientific_relevance: Hard-lit surface: pitch-black shadows with no fill, sunlit regolith with fine crisp footprints, black sky above a ridge.
production_influence: Strong reference for MOON_002/003: shadowed slopes go to near-black with a sharp lit/unlit boundary, horizon is a clean ridge line, ground texture is fine crisp pocks not sand ripples; shadow lengths show a lowish Sun.
notes: Reseau crosses are camera marks. Rover and astronaut are small and distant. Caption (not verified): Scott at the LRV at the edge of Hadley Rille.

title: Paranal opendome
camera_perspective: daytime 3/4-front exterior at ground level, enclosure shutter leaves slid apart, three people for scale
visible_characteristics: Daytime exterior of a large boxy rotating enclosure (VLT unit-telescope style): the upper structure is split into two tall white corrugated bi-parting leaves slid apart left and right, leaving a vertical slit through which the telescope structure (dark truss, ring, red-and-white instrument disc at the base of the opening) is visible; below is a cylindrical lower building with open louvres and a base platform; three tiny people at the left give scale; pale sunset sky. Sharp, orthographic-ish 3/4 side view.
scientific_relevance: Bi-parting shutter geometry: two flat panels slide sideways exposing a vertical slit over the telescope.
production_influence: Gives the open-slit end state of OBS_006 for a BOX enclosure: leaves are tall flat slabs that slide behind the fixed upper volume; slit is about 1/4 of the enclosure width; the telescope truss is seen inside. Note conflict: the manifest chose a hemispherical dome, this form is boxy.
credit_line: Author not stated in the Commons metadata I could read (licence CC BY-SA 3.0); attribution for reference use only
notes: Licence read from the en.wikipedia API file info (Commons page not reachable). Author field blank in the API: attribution unresolved, so do not use beyond reference. Source: Wikipedia Altazimuth mount article image list.

title: ESO-New Technology Telescope-phot-07b-07
camera_perspective: low-angle FRONT view at night looking up through an open slit; star field between the leaves
visible_characteristics: Night, low upward view at the front of a boxy enclosure of the NTT: two tall corrugated metal leaves lean/stand apart forming a V-shaped slit with deep-blue starry sky between them (a few bright stars visible). Inside the slit the telescope's large cream-coloured circular ring with a black truss/spider and the dark tube seen almost end-on from the front; a railing and red steps in front; shutter motors visible on the lower beam. The mirror itself is not visible, only the ring and centre box.
scientific_relevance: The telescope as seen through the opening: big circular ring, spider/truss, centre box; sky is a deep-blue gradient with a few stars.
production_influence: Best view of the slit-open state with the telescope visible through it and the camera looking up: leaves lean outward like a V, ring of the telescope is cream-coloured, mirror not visible; use for B01/B04 composition of aperture and slit.
notes: Licence CC BY 3.0 with author ESO read from the en.wikipedia API file info. Caption (not verified): ESO NTT at La Silla can observe very low on the horizon.

title: Moonset over ESO's Very Large Telescope
camera_perspective: telephoto ground view of a hilltop with four closed enclosures in front of the setting Moon
visible_characteristics: Very large orange full Moon (craters faintly visible as lighter/darker patches) sitting directly behind a small hilltop with four boxy white observatory enclosures and a small tower, all closed and tiny; pink-to-lilac dusk sky; the mountain slope in dark foreground. Telephoto; the Moon is far bigger than the buildings (scale is a lens compression effect).
scientific_relevance: Scale cue: a lens-compressed full Moon behind the observatory; enclosures are tiny.
production_influence: Composition reference for the Moon-over-observatory ground shot: the Moon is placed directly behind the buildings, orange near the horizon; buildings are small white boxes. Moon colour should be neutral when high.
notes: Licence CC BY 3.0, credit G.Gillet/ESO read from the en.wikipedia API file info. Telephoto compression exaggerates Moon size.

title: Diffuse reflection (multilingual SVG diagram)
camera_perspective: 2-D schematic: incident ray from the upper left onto a grainy surface, rays scatter in all directions
visible_characteristics: 2-D schematic in white with a grey polygon-grain surface at the bottom: a thick black incident-light arrow runs from the upper left down onto the surface, several blue 'primary' rays and cyan 'secondary' rays with filled arrowheads leave the surface in many different directions (some back up-left, some up-right) and a small fan of five open arrows at the upper right is labelled 'Scattered light'; legend dots for primary and secondary rays. Crisp vector lines, no shading.
scientific_relevance: Diffuse reflection: light is re-emitted in many directions, almost none back toward the source.
production_influence: Confirms OPT_007 grammar: a black incident arrow, blue/cyan scattered rays leaving at many angles and a small fan of open arrows labelled Scattered light; surface drawn as grey polygon grains.
notes: Recovered after a Wikimedia error page was saved as .svg.tmp (quarantined). File is the real SVG (sha256 of the SVG given) and its square QuickLook render is the viewed local PNG; the render crops the lower/right part of the drawing, so only the visible part is described. Licence read from the en.wikipedia API (CC BY-SA 4.0, author DnaX).

title: Starfire Optical Range sodium laser beam from an open-roof telescope
scientific_relevance: Very relevant composition: a single narrow beam leaving an open-roof observatory with the telescope pointing straight up.
notes: I downloaded and VIEWED this image (portrait, orange beam, telescope pointing up, two closed small domes) and then DELETED the file because the Commons metadata states only Public domain with no author, credit or source: provenance unclear, so it is link-only. The beam is a sodium-guide-star-type orange laser, not the green 532 nm ranging laser. viewed is false because no local file remains.

title: Histogram with a symmetric unimodal shape (bar chart, expected counts)
scientific_relevance: Generic bar-histogram style only (a peak with symmetric spread); NOT a photon-timing histogram.
notes: Licence read from the en.wikipedia imageinfo API. NOT DOWNLOADED (HTTP 429). A true photon-counting range histogram with a signal peak above flat background was not found under an open licence.

title: NASA Anticipates Lunar Findings from Artemis Retroreflector
camera_perspective: close side/3-4 view at eye level, hardware on a bench or spacecraft deck, shallow depth of field
visible_characteristics: A cylindrical grey metal housing capped by a bright red plastic protective cover (covers the optical face), under which a downward-pointing conical/pyramidal lower body (the cube apex side) hangs; the housing is held by two grey aluminium A-frame side brackets with lightening cut-outs and a short pivot pin/knob on the left; the bracket sits on a dark deck with a gold polyimide foil edge; thin wires (one white, one fine black loop) run around it; blurred benches behind. The optical face itself is not visible.
scientific_relevance: A modern successor retroreflector shows where the cube sits in its housing: the apex of the corner cube points down into the housing and the face sits at the top.
production_influence: Supports the depth of the cube in RETRO_003: the glass body is much deeper than the face and ends in an apex; a tilt pivot sits at the side of the mount (compare Apollo 14 tilt support).
notes: NOT an Apollo array (NGLR-1 flies on a 2025 commercial lander per the NASA caption, which I read). The red cap hides the cube face, so the pattern of faces is not visible. Observed vs assumed: that the conical body is the cube apex is my interpretation from the shape, not from a caption.

title: Escapement Time Pilot/Flieger quartz chronograph (dial, two sub-dials)
camera_perspective: low 3/4 front, wristwatch lying on its strap on a pale surface, slightly from below
visible_characteristics: A black dial with a ring of long and short luminous minute ticks, bold numerals only at 5 and 7 and bars/numerals at the other hours, a long white seconds hand and a shorter hour hand, two small round sub-dials (upper: 15-30-45-60 scale with its own thin hand; lower: 10-60 scale with a white tipped hand) and a small date window at 3 o'clock showing 15; a polished steel case with a large crown at top and two cylindrical pushers either side, mesh steel strap. The big seconds hand and sub-dial hands are clean, flat, high-contrast shapes.
scientific_relevance: Shows how a chronograph arranges a main seconds hand and two counters (minutes and a second register) for reading elapsed time.
production_influence: Dial-layout reference for the analogue variant of MG_001: flat white hands on black, tick hierarchy with every 5th tick longer, sub-dials with their own thin hands; two pushers and a crown on the case top are the stop/start/reset affordance.
notes: Licence CC0 and author read from the en.wikipedia imageinfo API. Wristwatch, not a stopwatch: same affordances (pushers) but small. Hands are not at a meaningful time.

title: Louis Moinet 'Compteur de Tierces' (first chronograph)
camera_perspective: straight-on front, black background, large hand-held timer (pocket-watch scale) with crown and pusher at top
visible_characteristics: A large circular silver-grey hand instrument on black: a plain engraved dial with an outer ring of 60 divisions numbered every 6 (60, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54), a very long thin blue steel hand from the centre across the whole ring, two small round sub-dials at the upper left and right each with a blue hand and a 60 scale, and a lower sub-dial with Roman numerals and a blue hand; a large ring crown and a separate cylindrical pusher at the top; a name engraved across the middle. Surface is matt and aged with speckled spots; rim is a plain polished band.
scientific_relevance: Historic chronograph for timing to a sixtieth of a second: relevant to the idea of a hand-held instrument measuring tiny time slices.
production_influence: Gives a non-wristwatch HAND-HELD timer silhouette (crown plus a side pusher on top, a full-length seconds hand over a divisions ring, two counters) for a vintage-style MG_001 variant; do not copy the name text. Not a modern stopwatch.
notes: Licence and author read from the en.wikipedia imageinfo API. Caption (not verified from the picture): the first ever chronograph. Original is 11.5 MB; saved copy is downscaled to 2400 px long side.

title: Eso-paranal-16
camera_perspective: wide interior 3/4 from the platform, telescope pointing steeply upward toward the open slit
visible_characteristics: Wide interior view (fisheye-like, stitched) of a VLT enclosure with the shutter slit open to a pale-blue sky: a big grey-silver altitude ring/fork and truss tube pointing steeply up toward the opening, a blue azimuth bearing and the red-and-white instrument disc at the Nasmyth platform, catwalks, ducts and louvres with warm yellow light coming through the walls. The curved interior wall and the stacked platforms show the building structure around the telescope.
scientific_relevance: How an alt-az tube pointing up sits inside the enclosure: altitude bearing and ring, truss, Nasmyth instrument disc, catwalks.
production_influence: Telescope-pointing-up reference for the B01 slit view: tube is a lattice of struts, altitude ring is a big pale-grey torus on a blue azimuth bearing, platforms ring the structure; slit lets sky light in from one side.
notes: Licence CC BY 4.0 read from the en.wikipedia API file info; stitched wide-angle panorama so straight lines bend slightly. Overlaps REF-OBS-011/TEL-004 in subject but adds the pointing-up/open-slit state.

source_org: NASA GSFC Scientific Visualization Studio (LRO LOLA/LROC data)
title: Full Moon (Moon Phase and Libration visualization frame)
camera_perspective: near-side full disc, north up, full phase; computer visualization from LRO data, not a photograph
visible_characteristics: Complete lit disc on black, sharp limb. Large dark grey maria blotches fill the upper left and the left-centre (a very big dark region with irregular edges), a smaller round dark mare near the upper-right limb, and mid-grey patches in the lower centre; the rest is pale grey-white highland full of craters, densest in the south (bottom). Bright ray craters stand out: one near the centre-left with long radial rays, plus a smaller one beside it and a bright dot near the left, which by position match Copernicus, Kepler and Aristarchus (not labelled in the source). Bright rays also fan from the bright southern region. Relief is flat at full phase, since the Sun is behind the viewer, with only the last few percent at the limb darker. The whole disc is neutral grey with a slight warm tint.
scientific_relevance: Near-side overview: maria (dark basalt plains) vs highlands (bright, older, crater-dense terrain); at full phase relief is hidden and albedo and rays dominate.
production_influence: Texture target for MOON_001: two-tone maria/highlands, strong ray systems, craters get denser toward the south. For the big full-disc beats, keep the shading subtle at full phase (flat), and use a strong terminator for any phase other than full.
credit_line: Credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio
notes: 2400x2400 JPEG saved unscaled. Computer visualization built from LRO LOLA topography and LROC colour data; it is not a photo. Saved file 2400x2400, 534462 bytes.

title: First Quarter (Moon Phase and Libration visualization frame)
camera_perspective: near-side disc, first quarter: right half lit, terminator running diagonally from upper centre to lower left
visible_characteristics: Right half of the disc is lit; the terminator is a slightly jagged, tilted line from the top centre-right down to the bottom-left (not vertical). Along the terminator, craters are shown with deep black shadows and bright rims, and relief is highly visible. Maria on the lit side are dark grey (large rounded one at the top right, a circular one at the right limb), highlands bright. The unlit left half is almost black but a faint dark-grey disc outline is still visible (earthshine-like rendering). The limb on the dark side is nearly invisible against black.
scientific_relevance: Terminator behaviour: sharp, irregular line, with craters on the terminator throwing long shadows; the lit half is always the Sun side.
production_influence: MOON_004 mask: hard-edged terminator, only a few pixels of softness (no atmosphere), slightly irregular because of relief; the terminator tilts as seen from Earth (here about 20-30 degrees from vertical). Unlit disc may carry a very faint dark-grey earthshine fill, not pure black, if the dark half should be seen.
credit_line: Credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio
notes: 2400x2400 JPEG saved unscaled. Visualization. Saved file 2400x2400, 311683 bytes.

title: Waxing crescent (Moon Phase and Libration visualization frame)
camera_perspective: near-side disc, waxing crescent; only a right-hand crescent lit
visible_characteristics: A thin lit crescent along the right edge, bounded on the left by a curved diagonal terminator. The dark disc is rendered as a nearly black, faint, round silhouette. The crescent shows pale grey highlands, a round dark mare at the right limb and a large darker region toward the centre, with craters and shadow-edged relief close to the terminator. The lit crescent is widest in the lower right.
scientific_relevance: Crescent geometry: the terminator is an ellipse (a projected great circle), not a circular arc cut from the disc.
production_influence: Crescent shape = the disc's outer limb circle minus an ellipse with the same height and a narrower width; the code mask should project the terminator as a half-ellipse, not move a circle across the disc (a common error).
credit_line: Credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio
notes: 2400x2400 JPEG saved unscaled. Visualization. Saved file 2400x2400, 212387 bytes.

title: Along the Lunar Terminator (art002e014045)
camera_perspective: oblique photo of the Moon's limb and terminator from the Orion window during the lunar flyby
visible_characteristics: A curved limb runs across the upper right with a black sky above. Most of the frame is the dark unlit Moon (barely distinguishable from the sky, but dark navy-black). The lit terrain shows craters whose floors are pitch black while their lit rims are thin glowing crescent edges; large crater floors appear as solid black ovals because the Sun is almost horizontal. Surface colour is brownish grey. Light falls off rapidly toward the lower left into total darkness, leaving only isolated lit ridges (bright dotted lines).
scientific_relevance: Real-photo terminator: hard shadows, floors in black, lit rims, and no soft transition.
production_influence: Terminator rendered in code should show the 'islands of lit rims' pattern if the texture has height data; with a plain colour texture, keep the terminator crisp, with a faint warm tint.
notes: Saved downscaled to 2400x1600 from 5568x3712. Saved file 2400x1600, 304634 bytes.

title: Craters Along the Lunar Terminator (art002e014055)
camera_perspective: oblique close-up of cratered terrain at the terminator; the limb curves across the top
visible_characteristics: Densely cratered grey-brown terrain curving away toward a black sky at the top. Low sun from the lower area leaves large crater interiors black and their opposite rims lit; small craters appear as bright arcs. The shadow boundary forms a ragged dark band in the lower half (black space below). A large flat-floored crater with a central peak and terraced wall sits at the upper right. Texture shows many overlapping craters of every size, with no smooth areas.
scientific_relevance: Crater population and shadow shapes under grazing light.
production_influence: Crater look for the globe: circular, overlapping, with floors in shadow under side light; helps match texture appearance for the highland areas.
notes: Saved downscaled to 2400x1600 from 5568x3712. Saved file 2400x1600, 489810 bytes.

source_org: NASA / Goddard / Arizona State University (LROC WAC)
title: The Far Side of the Moon - And All the Way Around
camera_perspective: far-side orthographic view centred at 180 deg longitude, 0 deg latitude; grayscale LROC mosaic
visible_characteristics: A full-disc grayscale mosaic that is uniformly covered by overlapping craters with very few dark patches (one dark, irregular small mare upper left, one tiny dark spot lower left); no large dark maria. Pole regions at the top and bottom show a pinched, mirrored pattern of stitching. Surface is uniformly mid-grey, much more even than the near side.
scientific_relevance: Shows why near-side maria identify the face: the far side has almost none.
production_influence: Reminder that the film's Moon must show the near side (maria visible) from the Earth view; the far side is irrelevant except when the Moon is seen from DSCOVR/Orion.
notes: 1600x1600 JPEG saved unscaled. Grayscale. Saved file 1600x1600, 1976919 bytes.

title: Copernicus Crater and The Lunar Timescale
camera_perspective: close-up (metres per pixel scale) of the rugged interior of Copernicus, high-resolution LROC NAC style
visible_characteristics: Grey monochrome terrain at close range: rough, hummocky surface scattered with thousands of angular boulders, the biggest clustering along ridge crests and slopes; hard black shadows are cast to the left, with sunlit slopes brighter on the right. The ground between boulders is a smooth grey fine-grained surface pocked with tiny craters. No horizon visible.
scientific_relevance: Fine regolith vs boulders under direct sunlight at crater scale, with shadows hard-edged and black.
production_influence: Rock sprite distribution: boulders cluster rather than scatter uniformly; shadows are pure black and hard-edged; ground texture is fine-grained grey.
notes: 1000x1000 JPEG saved unscaled. Page title names the crater; the scene shown is a close crop and the exact feature was not labelled on the page. Saved file 1000x1000, 153451 bytes.

title: Tycho Crater's Peak
camera_perspective: oblique LRO view of the central peak complex at lunar sunrise
visible_characteristics: A bright, steep, conical peak with long streaky downslope striations catches the light in the centre; an enormous perfectly black shadow of the summit falls toward the upper left; surrounding melt-floor terrain is hummocky grey with many black-floored hollows. The lit area fades into black at the lower right (the edge of illumination), and the frame is lit only by grazing sunrise light. Per the caption the peak complex is about 15 km wide, the summit 2 km above the floor, Tycho at 43.37 S, 348.68 E and about 82 km across.
scientific_relevance: Shadow length vs sun elevation on real relief: a 2 km peak casts a shadow many kilometres long at sunrise.
production_influence: Gives the real look of long shadows: pitch black, hard edge, no fill light; a low sun elevation multiplies shadow length (length = height / tan(elevation)).
notes: 2147x986 PNG (1.25 MB) saved unscaled. Saved file 2147x986, 1246671 bytes.

title: Astronaut Edwin Aldrin after deployment of EASEP on surface of moon (AS11-40-5948)
camera_perspective: ground-level 3/4 view looking across the site toward the lunar module and a low horizon
visible_characteristics: Square frame, black sky filling the top 40 percent, horizon almost flat and razor sharp at about 40 percent from the top. Foreground: grey-brown pebbly regolith with many bootprints, hundreds of small rocks and tiny shadows. Aldrin in a white suit at left, back to the camera; the instrument package (copper-coloured cylinder with silver wing panels) in the centre foreground; behind it to the left a smaller white framed panel on the ground tilted toward the sky, which the caption identifies as the Laser Ranging Retro-Reflector just behind the seismometer. The lunar module in the right midground with gold foil. The flag sits in the background centre, flying out horizontally on a rod, creased but not fluttering; a camera stand to its left. Small black crosses (reseau marks) are scattered over the image. Shadows are black and hard-edged, falling to the left/toward the camera.
scientific_relevance: The manifest's cited reference for the surface, horizon, props, flag. Confirms the reflector sits just behind the seismometer and that the sky is black with no stars or haze.
production_influence: Horizon: flat, razor sharp, black sky, no haze. Ground: grey-brown, finely pebbled with a gradient from big rocks at the foreground to fine texture at distance. Flag: extended horizontally by a rod, with creases, static. Shadows hard and black.
notes: Saved downscaled to 2400x2400 from 3904x3904. Describes the ground view requested in the manifest (MOON_002/003/005/006). Saved file 2400x2400, 1414239 bytes.

title: Close-up view of astronaut's footprint in lunar soil (AS11-40-5878)
camera_perspective: close-up oblique macro of the soil (70 mm lunar surface camera per the caption)
visible_characteristics: Black-and-white close-up of grey fine-grained soil, covered with tiny pebbles and clods; a bootprint in the lower right shows crisp tread ridges, with sharp-walled edges and a deep black shadow filling the heel. A larger angular rock lies upper left, casting a hard shadow to the left. Several black crosses (reseau marks) are overlaid in a grid. The soil has a cohesive, almost damp-sand look: the print holds its shape with vertical walls.
scientific_relevance: Regolith close-up: fine cohesive grains that hold a crisp print; pebbles and small angular rocks.
production_influence: Boot-print sprites should have crisp, near-vertical walls and visible tread with a deep black shadow; the soil texture should be fine-grained speckle, not smooth sand. Dust in the film must be ballistic, since the soil is fine and dry (MOON_007).
notes: Saved downscaled to 2390x2400 from 3896x3912. Monochrome. Saved file 2390x2400, 1273496 bytes.

title: Astronaut Alan Bean deploys Lunar Surface Magnetometer (AS12-46-6813)
camera_perspective: ground-level wide view across the site; low horizon about 40 percent down from the top, lunar module in the left background
visible_characteristics: Colour frame with a black sky filling the upper half, a nearly flat horizon at roughly 55 percent down the frame, and dark grey regolith in the foreground cut by many boot tracks and a long gold-and-brown cable running diagonally to the lower right. An astronaut in white stands near the horizon holding the instrument; the lunar module with a dish antenna is at far left. Craters of various sizes show as dark elliptical pools; the Sun is behind or beside the camera (soft dark shadows), a bright patch of light ground at right. Crumpled silver foil is in the lower left corner.
scientific_relevance: A second low-horizon viewpoint with different light (flat, with dark soil): shows how ground tone changes with sun angle.
production_influence: Ground brightness varies strongly with sun angle: with the Sun behind the camera, the ground is lighter and shadows are hidden; dark soil from this site looks darker than at Apollo 11. Foot-track texture adds scale (about 30 cm boot length).
notes: Saved downscaled to 2378x2400 from 5647x5699. The long-shadow target was NOT met by this frame; shadows here are short. Saved file 2378x2400, 1199819 bytes.

source_org: NASA / GSFC / Arizona State University (LROC NAC)
title: High Noon at Tranquility Base
camera_perspective: orbital top-down view of the Apollo 11 site with the Sun almost overhead; the scale bar is 200 m
visible_characteristics: Grey, nearly shadowless top-down view: ground is mid-grey with many small round craters of all sizes, bright at their rims. At far left a white dot with a small dark halo and a fine dark line marks the Apollo 11 site (label 'Apollo 11 Site'); a slightly brighter patch surrounds it. At the right edge, a large bright blast-pattern crater labelled 'West Crater' with bright rays and boulders. The scale bar labelled '200 meters' is about 375 px wide, so 1 px is about 0.53 m.
scientific_relevance: Gives the scale of the site: reading the on-image 200 m bar (375 px), the landing site to West Crater is roughly 1000 px, so about 530 m. The site is on a flat mare plain with small craters.
production_influence: Use as a locating reference: the Apollo 11 site is in a flat plain with small craters and a nearby bright crater (West) to the east. The reflector is a few metres across, sub-pixel here, so a ring marker in B05 should be drawn as a symbol, not a feature.
notes: 1400x1400 JPEG saved unscaled. The 530 m distance is my estimate from the on-image 200 m scale bar; not a published figure. Saved file 1400x1400, 282176 bytes.

Bright ray craters radiate white streaks (one at left of centre, one big one at the bottom-centre with many rays). The top and bottom strips are blurry and low-contrast (filler from a lower-resolution laser albedo map). The colour palette is a pale warm grey with subtle blue-brown differences in the maria.

title: Goddard Laser Ranging Facility directs a laser toward the Moon (Observe the Moon Night 2010)
camera_perspective: ground level, vertical frame, wide, looking up at the Moon; ground station platform lower right, small dome lower left
visible_characteristics: Vertical night frame. Two perfectly straight, thin, bright-green beams converge on a glaring white Moon with a star-burst flare (upper left). One beam rises almost vertically from a small white dome with its slit open (lower left, behind a black treeline); the other runs diagonally from a telescope on a white box-shaped ground-station platform at lower right (pinkish-red from a red work light; railings, a person at the rail, lattice fence at the bottom). The beams keep a constant width, have no visible spread, a slightly mottled core and a faint glow; sky is deep navy with a few stars; nothing else is illuminated by the beam.
scientific_relevance: Shows that a real visible-light laser beam IS visible from the side as a thin scattered line, but only in a long exposure and from a dark site; the film's pulse marker is an educational symbol, not a photograph.
production_influence: B01/B02: the Moon high in frame with the dome at the lower left matches the frame; B02's dashed floodlight must be drawn as a cone (the rejected idea), while real beams are razor thin. Never draw a continuous beam in B04.
notes: Long-exposure photo; NASA ~large derivative downloaded (not ~orig). Event: International Observe the Moon Night, 18 Sep 2010, Goddard Laser Ranging Facility (per NASA caption). Saved width after sips: 1370 px.

title: Visitors watch laser beams pointed at the Moon, Goddard Optical Site
camera_perspective: ground level, wide, low three-quarter on a small dome-on-box observatory at twilight
visible_characteristics: Wide twilight scene, royal-blue sky going near-black at the top. Moon (bright, soft halo) at upper right; a thin green beam runs from a small white hemispherical dome at left toward the Moon, a second beam crosses the top left corner. The dome sits on a beige one-storey cube building with an exterior stair and a rail around the dome base; the dome slit is open and faces the Moon. A white lattice tower with a small enclosed top and a second smaller closed white dome stand to the right; silhouetted people and a lit doorway in the foreground; dark conifer line on the horizon.
scientific_relevance: Documents a classic small dome-on-box observatory (hemisphere on a cuboid base with a stair and a rail ring) and how the beam appears at twilight: faint, thin, hardly brighter than the sky near the horizon.
production_influence: Pattern for OBS_001/OBS_002: low cuboid base, rail ring where the dome meets it, exterior stair, lit doorway as the only warm light. Use the dome-on-base proportion (dome diameter about equal to the base width).
notes: Long-exposure photo; NASA ~large derivative downloaded (not ~orig). Event: International Observe the Moon Night, 18 Sep 2010, Goddard Laser Ranging Facility (per NASA caption). Saved width after sips: 1920 px.

title: Double beams shoot into the night sky, Goddard Optical Site
camera_perspective: low angle, close, three-quarter on a hemispherical dome with the slit open
visible_characteristics: Low-angle close view of a white hemispherical dome on a rectangular concrete-looking roof. The slit is open on the upper left side: a vertical dark opening with a thin rim, a ring of green light along the inner edge of the slit (scattered laser light), and a wide soft-edged green beam fanning out of it towards the upper left (broad near the dome, about a quarter of the dome width, so a diverging beam, unlike the thin line at right). A second thin straight beam crosses the right of the frame from another source. The dome shows radial seams, a small hatch, a hinged shutter leaf standing proud of the shell, and a steel safety-rail frame at lower left. Sparse stars, deep blue sky.
scientific_relevance: Best photograph of dome + open slit + laser at once. Shows how the slit is a vertical cut through the dome from near the base to past the top, shutter leaf folded back over the shell, and that light spills on the slit rim.
production_influence: OBS_002/OBS_006 geometry: slit opening about one third of dome diameter in this view; shutter leaf sits proud of the shell (needs its own shadow-free layer and a small overlap strip). Dome seam ribs are a good cheap texture cue.
notes: Long-exposure photo; NASA ~large derivative downloaded (not ~orig). Event: International Observe the Moon Night, 18 Sep 2010, Goddard Laser Ranging Facility (per NASA caption). Saved width after sips: 1920 px.

title: Apache Point Observatory 3.5 m telescope running APOLLO (14 Sep 2005 per Commons)
camera_perspective: ground level, portrait, night, three-quarter on the corner of the tall enclosure
visible_characteristics: Portrait night frame at only 480x640 px. A bright Moon with lens flare (and a faint green horizontal streak) at upper left. At the right edge rises a tall light-grey building with flat angular walls and a rounded cylindrical lower part; a small projecting deck with a railing sticks out of its flank, a door sits at its base. A smaller dome with a railing is at the far left horizon. Pine trees in silhouette, grass in the foreground, a wooden sign post (text not legible at this size). Starry sky.
